# The fork, and how to move it onto a newer Cpp2IL

This tree is a fork of [Cpp2IL](https://github.com/SamboyCoding/Cpp2IL). What it adds is described in
`../../LocalPackages/README.md`, fix by fix. This file is about keeping it mergeable: where it starts from,
what it touches, and what to run when upstream moves.

## Where it starts from

| | |
|---|---|
| upstream | `https://github.com/SamboyCoding/Cpp2IL`, default branch `development` |
| base commit | `b20ca0d04f9d4deaf04636428b3c116589b2a167` |
| then | `97566c8`, `800cc39`, `e3aa824` from `https://github.com/AssetRipper/Cpp2IL` - the packaging commits that give the projects their `AssetRipper.` package ids |

Those four commits reconstruct the tree this fork was written against. `rebase-onto-upstream.sh` does it for
you and replays the fork on top of whatever upstream revision you ask for.

## How the fork is arranged

Almost everything it adds lives in files upstream does not have, so upstream can add, move and rewrite its own
code without meeting any of it:

* `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/*.cs` - the passes that turn lifted code back into something resembling the method
  that was written. `ForkPipeline.cs` is where they are ordered, and why each one runs where it does.
* `*.Fork.cs` - the fork's half of a class upstream also has. The upstream file gains the word `partial` and
  loses nothing else; every member the fork adds is in the sibling file.
* `Cpp2IL.Core.Tests/IlGeneratorForkTests.cs` - the fork's own tests.

What is left in upstream's own files is code that has to be there: a case in a switch, a call at the one point
in a pipeline where it belongs, a field read one way rather than another.

## What it changes in upstream's files

| file | what and why |
|---|---|
| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/NewArmV8InstructionSet.cs` | 55 arm64 mnemonics upstream does not translate, the shifted-register operand the architecture folds into a data-processing instruction, the comparison a later `b.cond` reads - taken *before* the arithmetic where `subs` writes the very register it compares, since `RecordComparison` emits moves rather than capturing values and would otherwise record a left side one subtraction too small (guarded by `Op0Reg == Op1Reg`: reordering it unconditionally costs seventeen of the corpus's twenty-five methods), the runtime method every managed method is handed, the width a store pair steps by, every register an argument could have arrived in handed to a call through a register rather than only the general purpose half, the zero register recognised as zero in the values a store pair writes, the address of a stack slot lifted as an address rather than as a read of the slot, and the register an address is indexed by kept rather than dropped at the `TODO` in the memory operand. Helpers are in `NewArmV8InstructionSet.Fork.cs`. Also two hooks: `ConditionalCompare` at the conditional compare and at each of the three places a held comparison becomes a value, and `VectorLanes` ahead of the mnemonic switch. One line at `UBFM`, handing the bitfield move to `BitfieldMove` (which is a shift in whichever direction its two immediates put it, and upstream translates only one of the two). Two further lines where an ADRP page is folded into a load: the offset scaled, because that fold never reaches `MemoryOperandFor` where every other addressing form is scaled, and the operand built by `ConstantBlobStore.Note` so the width of the load survives into the pass that needs it. Also the narrowing conversion the architecture folds into a data-processing operand - `add w8, w8, w0, uxtb` adds the low byte, not the word - materialised in `ShiftedOperand` via `ExtendedTo` in the fork, narrowing what goes in and widening straight back so the instruction's result stays a full word. **One line for an imported call.** A call to `sinf` or `memcpy` goes to a stub in `.plt` that no method table names, so it resolved to nothing and the statement was written out as `Method not found @4AFA510` - 523 sites over 51 addresses. `ImportedCall` in the fork file names it from the ELF and hands back the operands. It has to happen **here** rather than in a later pass: the fallback for an unknown callee hands over `x0` to `x7` and nothing else, and a floating point argument is in `v0`, so by the time the ISIL exists the argument is not among the operands at all. Only the imports that are exactly a managed method of the same shape - `modf` and `sincosf` answer through pointers, `memcpy` is a struct assignment rather than a call - and `__stack_chk_fail` is dropped outright, being what the guard branch calls when the stack has been smashed. **And a thunk is followed to what it jumps to**: three of the remaining addresses are one instruction long - `0x2183F68` jumping to `il2cpp_runtime_class_init_actual`, `0x2183F70` to `il2cpp_vm_object_box` - 90 sites between them, and `MetadataResolver` already knows those by name. **Never where the address is itself a key function.** Cpp2IL's key functions *are* thunks - `il2cpp_codegen_write_barrier` is `0x2183D8C`, `raise_exception` `0x2183DC4`, `SzArrayNew` `0x2183ED8` - and the resolver matches a call target against exactly those addresses, so following them unguarded moved every one off its own name at once: `full` 308 -> 271, roundtrip 1216 -> 897, decisions 96.6% -> 91.8%, the worst regression this fork has measured. **And a compare-and-exchange helper, recognised by shape rather than by address.** Every `event` accessor in the game compiles to the same loop - combine the delegate, then atomically install it and go round again if somebody got there first - and the install went to a helper no method table names: **62 sites at `0x21BC67C`, the largest unnamed target left**. `CompareExchangeOperands` names it `Interlocked.CompareExchange`, whose arguments are already in the right order. It is found by what the body does - it calls a primitive beginning with `casal`, the architecture's compare-and-swap, and carries a `dmb ish` of its own - so nothing is pinned to this binary. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/IlGenerator.Fork.cs` (`TypeOfOperand`) | An element of an array now answers with the array's element type, and a field of one with the field's, through the `ArrayElement` helper that was already there for `ldelem`. An element folded straight into an operand had no type at all, so `words[i] == null` loaded the constant zero as the number it literally is and then loaded the element at that width: `(long)words[i] == 0L`, which does not compile - and with it went the whole `foreach` body. Five commented statements in `Corpus::Tally` become the original source. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/IlGenerator.Fork.cs` (`LoadOperandInto`) | A zero moved into a place declared as a reference is `null`. That reading was refused here for a long time - a register the analysis calls a reference while in fact holding a number is common - but the alternative is not a number in a reference slot, it is **invalid IL**: `Expected O, but got I8`, 849 of them in the game, and ILSpy's own note predicts a lost statement seven times over. Extended to a local whose type was never worked out, which the emitter gives `System.Object` and so is the same place arrived at from the other side - but there only where **nothing does anything with the local except ask whether it is zero** (`OnlyAskedIfItIsNull`). Whichever it is, `null` and `0` answer that question alike, so nothing can be got wrong by choosing the one that compiles; reading every such zero as null instead costs three whole bodies and eleven commented statements. This is the compiler's cleared exception slot, and it is why `Corpus::SumSteps` threw where the original returned. The question is followed through a **copy** as well (1.11.1): destroying SSA leaves the answer a block away from the register that was cleared - `Corpus::Using` clears the slot in one block, an edge copy moves it into a second untyped local in another, and only that second local is compared against zero - so asking only about direct reads said no and the recovered `using` threw `OutOfMemoryException` where the original returned. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/SharedStandInRetyping.cs` | The **result** now takes the callee's declared return type as well as the arguments, unwrapping the `x8` memory operand to the place it was told to write. Without it a `Dictionary<string, int>.GetEnumerator` lands in a place still typed `Dictionary<object, int>.Enumerator`, `ResultFitsItsDestination` refuses the store, and the `foreach` walks an enumerator nothing ever assigned. The seed then travels the copy chain the pass already runs to a fixpoint. **Only works with the `StructSlotFields` guard beside it** - alone it was built twice and both times the whole loop was commented out. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/StructSlotFields.cs` | A slot may only be named as a field it could actually be (`CanBeTheField`). Containment was inferred from two frame offsets and nothing else, so a slot holding something of its own could be claimed as a field of whatever lay below it: in `Corpus::Tally` the enumerator's own slot sits eight bytes above a copy of itself and was named `_version`, an `int`, which turned the `foreach` into pointer arithmetic between two instantiations. A slot with no type is the shape this pass exists for; where it has one, that type is evidence and has to agree. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/FieldAddressRecovery.cs` | Also the address of a **static** field: `add v96, [v88 (Il2CppClass<T>) + 0xB8], 8` is where `Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref SomeEvent, ...)` gets the place it swaps. `MetadataResolver` already resolves the read half - `[storage + 8]` as a value - and only the address half was missing, which is the one every event accessor in the game needs: the call was named at 1.0.44x and its first argument was still `0 + 8L`. The generator writes it with `ldsflda`, which `TryLoadFieldAddress` could already do. **+27 whole bodies game-wide.** |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/LocalVariables.cs` | One condition on `PropagatePhi`: an untyped phi result takes a type from its inputs only where they **agree** about what they are. A register is taken back the moment the value in it is finished with, so a phi at a join often merges two unrelated things, and reading the type off the first input that has one gives the result whichever role happens to come first in the operand list. `InputsDisagree` in the fork asks the same question `CannotBeTheSameValue` already answers for a phi's edges. `full` 2749 -> 2750, commented 2324 -> 2314, one method gained on the source-free oracle and none lost. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/SsaForm.Fork.cs` | Two **numbers** meeting at a phi is ordinary, and for the same reason two references are: ISIL carries no width, so which integer type each end was given says more about which pass typed it than about what the register holds. `CannotBeTheSameValue` refused that edge as a register reuse, and the phi kept only the other side - `Corpus::Guarded` returns `10 / (n % 3)` on one path and `1` on the other, the divide's result was typed `Int64` against an `Int32` return, and the whole division died as unread while the method returned 1 for every input. Nothing marked it. The rest of the guard is unchanged: a number meeting a reference, or a struct meeting a different struct, is still a reuse. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/MetadataResolver.Fork.cs` | `PathIntoStructValue` answers for a distance that lands **inside** a field rather than on its front. `FieldOfStructValue` stops at the first field it does not land on, and a `foreach` over a dictionary reads through two levels: `Dictionary<K, V>.Enumerator._current` is a `KeyValuePair<K, V>`, so the key is the enumerator plus `0x10` and the value `0x18`, and neither is a field of the enumerator. `PathToNestedField` cannot answer either - it reads `BackingData.FieldOffset`, and both instantiations have their offsets laid out rather than recorded. `LaidOutSize` beside it measures a generic instantiation by laying its fields out, which is what says how far a field *reaches*; kept separate from `SizeOf` so the placement the two agree on does not change. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/StructSlotFields.cs` | A named slot also gives the path onward through a read **at a distance**: `pair.Key.Length` is `_current`, then `key`, then the string's `_stringLength`, and `PathToNestedField` supplies the last step from the field's own type. It also takes the field's type where it had none, so anything else reading through the slot knows what is there. Without both, the slot is left a bare local that nothing assigns, and the read compiles into a null dereference where it used to carry a marker and quietly answer nought. Also: slots are taken from the graph rather than from `method.Locals`, which holds only what the stack analysis registered at the start - the enumerator's own slot and the fields a callee wrote through it are made by the passes above and appear only as operands. Every version of a slot is named, not just the first. The enclosing struct is searched **nearest first**: single assignment form gives a copy of a struct its own slot a few bytes away, and a slot inside the nearer one is also some distance into the further one at a different field - `Corpus::Tally` named its key `_current.value` of the copy eight bytes below it. A slot inside a struct's struct becomes a `NestedFieldReference`. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/InaccessibleFieldRecovery.cs` | Each step of the chain gets a local in a register named `STEP` (`ChainStep`), which `IlGenerator.Fork.ReceiverLocal` then accepts as the receiver of the next accessor. Without that it made a fresh scratch local instead, so `enumerator.Current.Key` called `get_Key` on a `default(KeyValuePair<,>)` while `get_Current`'s answer went into a local nothing read. Reusing an *ordinary* local there is the thing `il2cpp-a-fresh-scratch-local-isolates-damage` measured as worse - a callee's mutation reaches every other statement sharing it - but a chain step is written once and read once by the two instructions this pass emits either side of it, so there is nothing for it to reach. Also: a chain of fields is reached one step at a time. The getter of the field at the end takes the field before it, not the object at the start, so `enumerator._current.key` has to become `enumerator.Current.Key` step by step or the property is called on the wrong thing. And a field written with **no prefix at all** - `KeyValuePair<K, V>.key`, `.value` - now looks for a property too: `Named` wanted `m_` or `_`, so those two stayed private and every statement reading them was commented out. The compiler's own backing fields are still left out, being found by their accessors instead. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/OutParameterWriteback.cs` | The clearing store is dropped where the zero arrives in a **register** rather than as the number nought, and the same test now decides which slots were *cleared alongside* one whose address is taken - it asked only about the number, so a struct cleared from a vector register contributed no offsets at all and every slot but the first kept its zero. The run that joins neighbouring cleared slots also allows a step of **16**: a word and a doubleword were allowed, but `stp v0, v0, [sp, #0x10]` names two slots 0x10 apart, so the run broke in the middle and the second half - which is where a `Dictionary<K, V>.Enumerator` keeps `_current` - stayed zero. `foreach (var pair in d)` read its key as `null`. Both tests are now one `ZeroStores`, worked out before the renaming moves the destinations from one prefix to the other. Also: A slot wider than a register is cleared from one - `movi v0.2d, #0` then `stp v0, v0, [sp, #0x10]` clears thirty-two bytes - so `IsZero` said no and the store stood. After the renaming above, the slot and the address register are one variable, so an assignment to the slot is an assignment to the address: everything that wanted the address read the cleared struct instead. `Corpus::Tally` handed `MoveNext` a zero and threw; `GetEnumerator`, `MoveNext` and `Dispose` now name one slot. Which registers hold zero is carried along the block, as `ConstantFolding` does, so nothing is assumed about how control reached it. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/StackProtectorRemoval.cs` | **New.** The compiler wraps a method holding an array on its frame in a stack protector: the prologue copies a cookie out of thread-local storage - offset `0x28` of the thread pointer, bionic's `TLS_SLOT_STACK_GUARD` - and the epilogue checks it is still there. Nobody wrote it and recovered C# has no stack to smash, but the `__stack_chk_fail` it guards is already dropped in the lifter, so what was left was a comparison of two places recovery cannot name: two `Unmanaged memory load` markers and an `if` around whatever followed. Both halves must match - a thread-local slot against a frame slot, deciding a branch into a block that is empty or a single `Throw` - which is what makes it safe; either read on its own is an ordinary field or local. Runs **last**: the shape only exists once the frame slots are named and the two reads have been propagated into the comparison, and placed beside `NullCheckRemover` it matched nothing at all. `unmanaged` 1323 -> 1259. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/DeadCodeEliminator.cs` | A local holding an `Il2CppClass` pointer, passed to a **named** runtime helper, does not count as a read. Boxing, unboxing, a cast and an allocation are all emitted from that operand's own **type**, never from its value - the same reason the static-storage pointer beside it does not count - so the two reads that loaded it (the metadata table out of a `.got` slot, then the class out of the table) are dead and were standing in the recovered method as `Unmanaged memory load`. Only the class stand-in: a `MethodInfo` in the same position is sometimes a real managed argument, and dropping its read would put a silently wrong value where a marker was. `unmanaged` 1612 -> 1323 game-wide, `full` 2657 -> 2724. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/NewArmV8InstructionSet.cs` | Two more, both about a width or a flag the architecture has and ISIL does not. **The carry is a second reading of the same flags.** `HI`/`CS`/`CC`/`LS` ask an *unsigned* question, and after an **addition** the carry is not a fact about the result at all - `csel w8, w9, w8, hi` following `cmn w8, #32` was rendered as `(w8 + 32) > 0`, the inverse of what it asks, and `Corpus::Bits` returned `0x55C00000055` where the source says `0x70000055`. `RecordComparison` now seeds a second pair of pseudo-registers, `RecordCarry` (fork) overwrites it for a 32-bit addition of an immediate with the exact unsigned question `(uint)wn >= 2^32 - imm`, and the four consumers take the pair the condition belongs to via `ComparisonSide` (fork). 250 sites in the game. **And a widening multiply multiplies words, not registers.** `smaddl`/`smull` sign-extend their two 32-bit sources and `umaddl`/`umull` zero-extend them; lifted as a plain multiply of 64-bit locals, a magic-division constant assembled by `movz`/`movk` reads as 2216757315 rather than -2078209981, and every remainder by a constant came out wrong. `WidenedSource` (fork) writes the extension as a shift pair, which `ConstantFolding` collapses back to one number wherever the source is the constant these instructions exist for. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/SwitchTableRecovery.cs` | **New.** A `switch` whose cases are dense and whose arms are constants becomes a table in the binary's own data, which resolves to nothing - so the method answered with its default for every input. The address is a constant once the page and offset are folded, the count is in the comparison guarding the read, and the width is the index scale; the answers are read back and become a chain of choices. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/ConstantFolding.cs` | **New.** A constant too wide for one instruction is built a sixteen bit field at a time, so what reaches the analysis is a chain of masks and ors. The decompiler folds it at the end, which is why the output never looked wrong - but no pass in between could read the number. Folds only where every source is already a constant, carrying them along the block itself so it does not depend on which propagation runs next. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/Aapcs64.cs` | `ReturnsIndirectly`: a composite over sixteen bytes is not returned in a register - the caller passes somewhere to write it in `x8`. Sizing has to add the fields up for a generic instantiation, which records no size of its own and carries **no fields of its own** either, so they come off `GenericInstanceTypeAnalysisContext.GenericType`. A homogeneous float struct is the architecture's exception and is excluded. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/NewArmV8InstructionSet.cs` | **One line in `AddCall`**, beneath upstream's own `//TODO Do certain value types have different return registers?`: a struct whose every field is a float is returned one field per vector register, and naming the result `x0` meant single assignment form never gave `v0..v7` a new value at a call - so the caller's own parameters, which arrive in those same registers, went on reaching every read below it. `worldPos - _camTransform.position` came out as `worldPos.x - worldPos.x`, zero, with no marker, in 16 places. `VectorReturnFields` (fork) yields one instruction per returned field, written as a **read** of the answer (`[x0 + 4]`) rather than a copy of it - a copy is folded away by propagation, which is how the three earlier attempts at this family died. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/IlGenerator.cs` | Also: one call to `ConvertToWidthOf` (fork) after the operand switch. ISIL has no width, so a local settled as `Int64` was pushed as one into a 32-bit place and the IL was unverifiable. Widening only - narrowing is done on a width the *analysis inferred*, and where that is wrong the value is destroyed: it took `Corpus::Mix` from 321186724655 to -935822545 and the execution oracle from 38/43 to 37/43. The *source* side is asked through `TypeOfOperand`, not required to be a local: a field and an array element state their width in the metadata just as flatly, and restricting it to locals left every field and element load unconverted (`Expected I8, but got I4` 70 to 54, total notes 1261 to 1245, every other measure identical). A constant is asked the same question by `EmittedAsThirtyTwoBits`: only the 64-bit cases here choose a width from the place they are going to, while `int`, `uint`, `short`, `byte` and `bool` emit `ldc.i4` whatever they meet (`Expected I8, but got I4` 54 to 44). **Both width changes are honest about what they bought: 26 notes between them and not one recovered statement** - every outcome measure was byte-identical across both rounds. Kept because they are monotone and free, not because they won anything. Also: one call to `CountTheBoundaryCrossings` (fork), which is inert unless `BOXTRACE` is set and only reports - it exists because the obvious `box`/`unbox.any` at the same point is wrong, and the counts say why. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/NewArmV8InstructionSet.cs` | Also: two call sites take `GetCallResultOperand` (fork) instead of `GetReturnRegisterForContext`, which is where upstream's own `//TODO Do certain value types have different return registers?` sits. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/IlGenerator.cs` | Also: the call's result is stored only when `ResultFitsItsDestination` (fork) agrees. Inside a shared generic the destination is typed by the stand-in `Dictionary<int, object>` while the call returns the real instantiation, and storing across that reads back as a cast C# refuses - which cost `BoardController::ComputeHighlights` all fifty of its branches before the guard existed. **Two one-line guards for `ldflda`.** A value type's method is called on the address of one and a by-reference parameter wants an address, and both answered with the address of a **local** - which is all `ReceiverLocal` and `ScratchLocal` can make. Where the thing in that position is a field the local is a *copy*: what the callee writes lands in the copy and the field never changes. `TryLoadFieldAddress` in the fork file emits `ldflda` (or `ldsflda`) instead, and only where the base's type actually declares the field - `LoadLocal` matches a local to a parameter by name, so an `ldflda` of a field the stack type does not declare is invalid IL. Inert on its own: what produces field references in those positions is `FieldAddressRecovery`. Also one case in the key-function emission for `il2cpp_vm_object_box`, which is what a thunk-followed call reaches: the same `box` instruction as `il2cpp_codegen_box` beside it, but with **the arguments the other way round** - the runtime entry point takes the class first, while the `codegen` shape is built by `CastHelperRecovery` with the value first. Without it the boxing sites the thunk opens up come out as `Unknown call target operand` and cost six whole methods. And one condition on the case that loads a type used as a value: where the place it is going declares a `RuntimeTypeHandle`, it is `ldtoken` rather than a native-integer zero. `typeof(X)` is two instructions in C# and **both already survived** - the analysis resolves the token and the ISIL reads `Call Type.GetTypeFromHandle, v218, typeof(UnityEngine.RectTransform)` - so the generator was the only thing missing it, and 43 sites came out as `Type.GetTypeFromHandle((RuntimeTypeHandle)0)`, every one a commented statement. Narrow because a type operand is far more often a class pointer the runtime is handed, which *is* a native integer; the parameter's own type is what tells the two apart. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/LogicalShift.cs` | **New.** arm64 has two right shifts - `LSRV`/`UBFM` bring in zeroes, `ASRV`/`SBFM` bring in the sign - and ISIL has one `ShiftRight` for both, which the generator emitted as `Shr`. So every logical shift came back arithmetic: identical on a non-negative value, wrong on every negative one, with no marker and no commented statement. `probeg shifts` counts **93 logical against 17 arithmetic** in Assembly-CSharp (4153 against 620 binary-wide). Marks are held in a `ConditionalWeakTable` rather than as an operand, because `ConstantFolding` refuses anything whose operand count is not three. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/BitfieldMove.cs` | Its `emit` delegate hands back the instruction it created, so the extract half can be marked as logical when the mnemonic is `UBFM`. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/NewArmV8InstructionSet.cs` | Also: `LSRV` split out of the case it shared with `ASRV`, so the logical one can be marked. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/LocalVariables.cs` | One line beyond what is listed elsewhere: the call-argument typing uses `SetTypeFromParameter` (fork) rather than `SetTypeIfUnknown`. A register reused across a join is typed by whichever edge the inference reached first, and once it has *any* type the parameter it is passed as cannot correct it - one local written from six places, three arrays and three lists, came out as `Il2CppMethodInfo`, which managed code never holds. The fork overrules a runtime stand-in with the declared parameter type, **except inside a generic body**, where the method's own `MethodInfo*` is what every runtime generic context entry is reached through: overruling it there emptied four generic extension methods. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/InlinedConstructorRecovery.cs` | **New.** A constructor small enough to inline leaves the allocation, the base constructor call and the field writes its body did - and those fields are the callee's own and often `readonly`, so no C# expresses them. The allocation still compiles, so nothing marks it and the object simply holds the wrong values: `Corpus::Areas` answered 13 where the original answers 83200. Matches each write to the parameter that stands for it (field name without `_`/`m_`, plus type) and folds only when every parameter is matched exactly once. Built **at the last write**, not at the allocation, because an argument is often computed between the two; and the base constructor call is nopped, since the generator only looks forward for one to fuse. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/UnboxRecovery.cs` | **New.** The unboxing helper and the cast helper have the same call shape, so `CastHelperRecovery` names both `isinst` - and adding an object to an int is not C#. What separates them is that **nobody dereferences the result of a cast**: a result only ever read at offset zero, for a value type, is a box being opened. Retypes the result, replaces `[result]` with `result`, and renames the call so the generator writes `unbox.any`. Only when every use is such a read. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/NewArmV8InstructionSet.cs` | **One line wrapping the frame-slot offset in `Scaled` (fork).** A memory operand based on register 31 becomes a `StackOffset`, and that path took `MemOffset` raw while `MemoryOperandFor` beside it scales - so every 128-bit access to the frame named a slot at a *sixteenth* of its offset, and a `q` spill and its reload disagreed about which slot they meant. `GizmosDrawer::DrawPoint` read two of a `Vector3` parameter's three lanes back as `default(float)`. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/IlGenerator.cs` | **One line calling `TryThrowTheObject` (fork)** in `case OpCode.Throw`. The opcode carries a *type* and the generator makes a fresh instance of it, which is right for the throws the runtime raises on its own account and wrong for every `throw new Foo(message)` the program wrote: there the object exists already, with its message in it. `ThrowTheConstructedException` (fork) puts the object on the opcode where a constructor call reaches the throw and nothing else reads it; this loads it. |
| `Cpp2IL.Core/IlGenerator.cs` | **One line calling `AddCatchClauses` (fork)**, last of `GenerateIl`. il2cpp compiles `catch (T)` into a raise and a C++ landing pad, and clang lays the pad in the instruction stream like any other code - so the whole handler is already in the graph, and the only thing missing is that a CIL `throw` ends the block, so the decompiler discards it as unreachable with no marker on any scorer. `CatchClauses` (fork) recognises the pad, names the caught type from the `Il2CppClass<T>` operand the analysis already types, deletes the plumbing and moves the handler to the end of `graph.Blocks`; this writes the `CilExceptionHandler`, the `pop` a handler is entered with, and the `leave` that replaces every `ret` in it. The `try` range is the throwing block alone - the real range is in `.gcc_except_table`, which this does not read. Each was written to refuse to carry a field read past a write to that field and neither ever did. `StoreTarget.Of` answers off the opcode instead, and both now ask that; `IsConstantValue` is deliberately untouched, since it drives `Sources`, dead code elimination and the stack analysis. `Corpus+<Steps>d__73::MoveNext` is the shape: an iterator state machine loads `<>1__state`, stores -1 over it, and then compares the loop counter in the very register the load left it in - so the comparison read the field a second time and got -1, and the first element of every `yield` loop came out `(-1)*(-1)` rather than `0*0`. Whole, no marker, rated `full`. Also: a store through a **raw memory operand** now invalidates a field read, since field recovery does not name every write and the same slot appears as `[x0 + 0x10]` on one line and as `this.<>1__state` on the next; and the two field references are compared through `IsTheSameField` rather than by object, for the reason that helper gives. Corpus oracle 60 -> 62 of 79. On the game, taken against the same build with `STALEREAD_OFF=1`: compare2 full, allscore, decisions, roundtrip and genfail all level, `cfscore` 608/7 -> 607/8 and `unmanaged` 316 -> 324 - the trade RECOVERY.md names, a read becoming a marker rather than quietly answering with the wrong value - and `livecount` **live +7, branches +1**, the live lines that left being `_ = list.Count;` discards. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/InstructionSets/NewArmV8InstructionSet.cs` | Also: **one line at `MOV` for a bitmask immediate the disassembler cannot render.** `mov x9, #-4294967296` is `orr x9, xzr, #0xffffffff00000000` - the same encoding `LogicalImmediate` already decodes for `and`/`orr`/`eor`. Disarm gives the mnemonic and then an operand it cannot represent (`Op1Kind` is `Register`, `Op1Reg` is `INVALID`), so the lifter moved a local **nothing ever assigns** and everything computed from it was arithmetic on nothing. `MovedBitmask` (fork) decodes it, and only where the raw word really is `orr Xd, XZR, #imm` and the disassembler gave no operand of its own. **65 sites in 58 methods** (`probe2 badoperand`, new - distinct from `invalid`, which counts words refused outright and is all NEON), `Buffer::MemoryCopy` and `MulticastDelegate::CombineImpl` among them. `Corpus::Reversed` is the shape: counting an index down is done in the **high half** of a register - `x10 = len << 32`, `x10 += (-1 << 32)` each turn, `asr #30` reading the index back already scaled by four. All 65 are in the substituted assemblies, so every scorer is identical; the evidence is the ISIL. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/StandInCopyType.cs`, `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/GenericSharingRecovery.cs` and two lines in `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/ForkPipeline.cs` | **A local whose every definition is a copy does not keep a generic-sharing stand-in either.** `StandInCopyType` already overrules a `Il2CppClass<T>` stand-in that only ever arrived by copy; the *other* stand-in needs the same treatment for a different reason. il2cpp shares one body per reference instantiation, so every call into `List<T>` names its receiver `List<object>` and that type settles on the local. While copy propagation folded the field read into the call the receiver kept the field's real type and nothing noticed; once a copy legitimately survives (see `StoreTarget`) the local keeps `List<object>`, `get_Item` answers `object`, and a field of the element has nothing to resolve against - `BoardController::InitBoard` wrote **every target colour as zero**, where the source says `_targetColors[i] = _targets[i].color`. Three links, each inert alone and measured so: `SharperInstantiation` gives the local its real instantiation back; `GenericSharingRecovery` now retypes the call's **result** as well as its receiver; and `GenericSharingRecovery` plus `MetadataResolver.ResolveFieldOffsets` are re-run after `StandInEdgeCopy`, for exactly the reason the array passes already are re-run there. `SharperInstantiation` is exact rather than heuristic - the same generic definition, argument for argument, differing only where the stand-in has a stand-in and the copy has something real, and `System.Object` standing where a **value type** is refused, since a value-type instantiation gets a body of its own and is never shared with one. Repays the whole `compare2`/`allscore` cost of the stale-read guard: full 2560 -> **2561**, allscore 2120 -> **2121**, cfscore 607/8 -> **608/7**, unmanaged 324 -> 323, everything else level, and `InitBoard` is the only verdict that moves. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/BoxedIsAnObject.cs` (**new**), one call in `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/ForkPipeline.cs`, and `Trace` in the same file | **What a box answers with is an `object`.** `object o = flag ? (object)"text" : (object)7;` merges a string with a boxed `int` in one register; the string arm types it `System.String` first, that reaches the box's result through the copies, and `SetTypeIfUnknown` will not revisit one - so the boxed seven is written `string text2 = (string)(object)7;` and throws on a cast the source never had, with the `isinst` below it recovered perfectly and never reached (`Corpus::AsOrNull`). Overrules **only** a reference type a boxed value can never be: `object`, `ValueType`, `Enum`, an interface and a generic parameter are all left alone, because the read-through-a-cast family depends on them. Every scorer identical and one line of the game better; it is link one of three and the other two are named in ROUND-LOG.md. Gated `BOXEDOBJECT_OFF=1`. Also `ForkPipeline.Trace`, called from all six hooks and silent unless `PIPETRACE` matches the method name: printing the body at each hook is what found the `ClearAndSet`/`Describe` root in one run instead of a bisection, and it is the instrument `il2cpp-the-dump-is-not-where-the-pass-runs` asks for. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/TypeTestNarrowing.cs` (**new**), one call each in `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/ExactTypeTestRecovery.cs` and `InlinedTypeTestRecovery.cs`, and `WidenWhatCarriesIt` in `BoxedIsAnObject.cs` | **The other two thirds of `object o = flag ? (object)"text" : (object)7;`, which only work together.** Retyping the box (the row above) changed nothing the output could show, because the phi it feeds still said `System.String` and the copy into it was written as a cast - so `WidenWhatCarriesIt` widens whatever a boxed value is merged into, bounded to the copy closure of the boxes just retyped rather than stated over every phi that sees an `object`: widening is safe for the language and expensive for the recovery, so it is only done where the type that is there is known to be wrong. And then the tested value has to stop being read below the test: both type-test passes put back the `isinst` and give its answer a local of its own, and neither says what that answer is **for** - the machine keeps the object in the same register either way, so `String::ToUpperInvariant` was called on the object. Invisible while the tested value happened to be typed as the target, fatal the moment it is typed honestly, which is why the two halves had to land in one round. `TypeTestNarrowing` replaces reads of the tested value with the narrowed one only in a region entered nowhere else - the success successor, then any block every one of whose predecessors is already in the region - which is dominance computed as it is needed rather than out of `DominatorInfo`, built before the guard remover changed the edges. Corpus oracle 62 -> 63 of 79 and every game scorer identical. Gated `TYPETESTNARROW_OFF=1`. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/StaticStorageIsTheFirstField.cs` (**new**), one call in `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/ForkPipeline.cs` | **Every event accessor in the game was swapping a throwaway.** `FieldAddressRecovery` reads `Add v121, [klass + 0xB8], 8` as `&Type.someStatic` and writes `ldsflda`; its own remark names the caller it exists for - `Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref SomeEvent, …)`, which every event accessor is. But **the first static field is at distance nought, so there is no addition** and that pass never sees it: the storage local goes straight into the call, the callee's signature retypes it `System.Object&`, and the generator writes `object location = default(object);` and swaps that. The combine, the type test and the retry are all recovered perfectly around it and the event is never written. Only a **by-reference** parameter, and only where the owner declares a static field at nought - a static storage block reaching an ordinary parameter is the runtime pointer it is. Runs in `BeforeUnusedLocalsAreDropped` (found with `PIPETRACE`): by the last hook the local has been retyped from the callee's signature and no longer says whose storage it is. No scorer can see this, so the observable is the output: `CompareExchange(ref location …)` **10 sites -> 0**, and `CompareExchange(ref …Unsafe.As(ref TheField) …)` 50 -> 60. Every game scorer identical. Gated `STATICREF_OFF=1`. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/CachedDelegateRecovery.cs` | Also: **the fold is declined where it would make two sites mean two fields.** The pass makes a cached lambda's use name the field so the decompiler folds test/build/store/use back into a lambda literal - and the decompiler folds only what it can see, so a **second** read of the same field elsewhere in the method is left bare. Once the export is recompiled those two sites name two different fields: `Adjust += (int v) => v + 5;` gets a fresh cache of the new assembly's own while `Adjust -= <>c.<>9__86_0;` still names the original, which nothing now writes, so `Delegate.Remove(list, null)` removes nothing and the event stays subscribed. `ReadElsewhere` counts the field's reads outside the two definitions - one is the pattern's own test, anything beyond it is a use the fold cannot reach - and declines, leaving the local in place so both sites name the one field again. `Corpus::EventRoundTrip` 105 -> 1105. On the game **decisions 1326 -> 1328** and **livecount live +49, branches +15**, everything else level; the cost is legibility, 50 more places showing the compiler's cache instead of a lambda literal, in about 25 methods that all had the same latent bug. Gated `CACHEDLAMBDA_OFF=1`. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/UnscaledSubscript.cs` (**new**), one call in `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/ForkPipeline.cs` | **An index the addressing mode does not scale is a byte offset, not a subscript.** A loop counting an index *down* keeps it in the high half of a register and lets one shift do the scaling as well - `add x12, x19, x10, asr #30`, where 30 is `32 - log2(stride)` - so what reaches the addressing mode is a byte offset with no scale on it, and reading it as a subscript is four times too far (`Corpus::Reversed`, `IndexOutOfRangeException` on every input). Written by moving the scaling **out of the shift** rather than by dividing: `x >> 30` used as a byte offset with stride 4 is `x >> 32` used as a subscript with scale 4, exactly, and it costs no instruction. Narrow on purpose - only where the index's one definition is a right shift and the index has one use - because the general case needs a division emitted, and the general case is where widening this path cost twelve game methods before. Corpus oracle 64 -> 65 of 79; **zero files differ in `Assembly-CSharp`**, which has none of this idiom. Gated `UNSCALED_OFF=1`. |

| `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/TheBufferIsTheWholeStruct.cs` (**new**), one call in `Cpp2IL.Core/Analysis/ForkPipeline.cs` | **A struct returned through `x8` fills the whole slot, not the field at the front of it.** A composite over sixteen bytes is returned indirectly and the binding already works - the call's destination is the slot - but that destination is a memory write at distance **nought**, and field resolution names distance nought of a struct as its first member. So `Call List<int>::GetEnumerator, v42._list, values` writes the enumerator into `._list` and `MoveNext` then runs on a slot nothing wrote: the recovered source calls `GetEnumerator()`, throws the answer away and iterates `default(List<int>.Enumerator)`, which is empty, so the loop never runs. Every `foreach` over a `List` or a `Dictionary` was that. Exact rather than a guess about what a distance means - only where the callee **returns indirectly** and the slot is declared as the type it returns - so `FrontMember`, which named it, is right everywhere else. Corpus oracle 65 -> 67 of 79 (`Total` and `Tally`). No scorer can see it, so the observable is the output: discarded `x.GetEnumerator();` statements **19 -> 9** and `Enumerator … = default(…)` **46 -> 36**. `commented` 371 -> 378 in one method - the stand-in seam from the other side - and `livecount` -32 live, which is junk going away: `RendererExtension::IsVisible` becomes `return GeometryUtility.TestPlanesAABB(_frustumPlanes, renderer.bounds);` from four lines that passed `default(Bounds)`. Gated `BUFFERWHOLE_OFF=1`. |

Where the fork needed a different signature it added a method beside the original, so that a merge does not
have to reconcile two versions of one declaration. **Two private ones escaped that rule and are still to be
undone**: `Analysis/MetadataInitGuardRemover.cs::TryRemoveGuard` gained `float metadataVersion, bool is32Bit`,
and `Analysis/LocalVariables.cs::InstantiatedType` gained an optional `definitions` dictionary with its one
upstream call site rewritten to pass it. Both are `private static`, so a rebase conflict in either is confined
to its own file, but neither should have been edited in place.

## Moving onto a newer upstream

```sh
External/Cpp2IL/rebase-onto-upstream.sh /tmp/cpp2il-rebase           # onto upstream's development
External/Cpp2IL/rebase-onto-upstream.sh /tmp/cpp2il-rebase v2026.1.0 # or onto a tag or commit
```

The script clones upstream, reconstructs the base commit above, commits this tree on top of it as a single
commit, and rebases that commit onto the revision you asked for. Whatever conflicts are left are ordinary
rebase conflicts in the files listed in the table - resolve them there, then:

```sh
cd /tmp/cpp2il-rebase
git rebase --continue
dotnet test -c Release
rsync -a --delete --exclude .git --exclude TestFiles --exclude bin --exclude obj \
    --exclude FORK.md --exclude rebase-onto-upstream.sh \
    /tmp/cpp2il-rebase/ External/Cpp2IL/
```

`FORK.md` and `rebase-onto-upstream.sh` are this repository's, not the fork's, so they have to be excluded -
`--delete` removes anything the source tree does not have, and it has neither of them.

Then raise `VersionPrefix` in both csproj files and the `Version` in
`Source/AssetRipper.Import/AssetRipper.Import.csproj`, repack into `LocalPackages`, and record the new base
commit at the top of this file.
